CyteTypeR is the R client for [CyteType](https://github.com/NygenAnalytics/CyteType). It prepares a clustered Seurat object, submits an annotation job to the CyteType API and adds the returned annotations to the object.

The full documentation for the R and Python clients is at <https://docs.nygen.io/CyteType/>. Start with the [R quickstart](https://docs.nygen.io/CyteType/getting-started/quickstart-r/), which annotates the 10x Genomics PBMC 3k dataset step by step. The code on this page is not run when the vignette is built.

## The workflow in brief

Sign in once on each computer. This opens CyteType sign-in in your browser and saves an API key locally:

```{r}
library(CyteTypeR)
SetupCyteTypeR()
```

Then prepare a normalized, clustered Seurat object and its marker table (from `Seurat::FindAllMarkers()`), and submit the job:

```{r}
prepped_data <- PrepareCyteTypeR(
  obj = pbmc,
  marker_table = pbmc.markers,
  group_key = "seurat_clusters",
  coordinates_key = "umap"
)

pbmc <- CyteTypeR(
  obj = pbmc,
  prepped_data = prepped_data,
  study_context = "Peripheral blood mononuclear cells from a healthy human donor",
  metadata = list(title = "PBMC 3k")
)
```

Every cell now has its cluster's label, Cell Ontology term, cell state and reviewer confidence in `pbmc@meta.data`, and `pbmc@misc$cytetype_results` has one row per cluster:

```{r}
head(pbmc@meta.data$cytetype_annotation_seurat_clusters)
GetResults(pbmc)
```
